blocks.text: The clone didn't cross straight away. First he wrote a long letter, one of those that bring not a ground but an explanation, and Andrés received it in the boat, with the engine off in the middle of the plate.
blocks.html: The clone didn't cross straight away. First he wrote a long letter, one of those that bring not a ground but an explanation, and Andrés received it in the boat, with the engine off in the middle of the plate.

blocks.text: *I don't want you to call it a miracle,* the other wrote, and Andrés thought it with him. *I want you to know what is taken apart. A body is an order: not only flesh, but also the way the particles were arranged, the heat, the scar, the salt on the skin, the memory, if memory is also an order. The machine doesn't send the weight the way you send a bundle. It names the order, and in naming it, undoes it. On the other side, another machine hears the name and puts each thing back in its place, or in a place so similar that a man can walk and ask for water. The original doesn't remain, because the name can't be spoken twice at once: if it remained, there would be two orders, and that, they say, the machine won't allow. Nothing is lost: the energy continues, the order travels. What is interrupted, though, is the while of being a place.*

blocks.text: Andrés looked at the water, which was a place, and imagined himself not being one. It gave him a cold that wasn't from the levante.

blocks.text: That night he told Aya and Lía, word for word, or as many words as he could bring back without them turning into a brochure. Lía listened with his own eyes, patient, and didn't soften the phrase.
blocks.html: That night he told Aya and Lía, word for word, or as many words as he could bring back without them turning into a brochure. Lía listened with his own eyes, patient, and didn't soften the phrase.

blocks.text: “So when you cross, you stop being a place,” she said. “There's a while, Nuria's hollow, when you're neither in the hangar nor at El Estacio. The energy, all right, hasn't been lost. And you? Are you energy, Father, or are you the while? I come to an end, and my coming to an end is a while that closes. This machine closes one while and opens another, and says it's the same because the order matches. I'm not sure an order is a father.”

blocks.text: Andrés wasn't offended. He sat down on the rush-seat chair, the usual one, and felt its arms, the old rope, the wood.
blocks.html: Andrés wasn't offended. He sat down on the rush-seat chair, the usual one, and felt its arms, the old rope, the wood.

blocks.text: “When I receive a letter, I'm still a place, and a world reaches me,” he said. “Now they're asking me to stop being a place in order to be a world. It's the other way round. It makes me dizzy. It also gives me, I won't deny it, an old longing: to see with these feet what I've drunk with my memory. To see it with him. For the two of us to sit down, not facing the sea at a departure, but in this kitchen, after one of us has been undone and made again.”

For the two of us to sit down, not facing the sea at a departure, but in this kitchen, after one of us has been undone and made again.”

blocks.text: Aya, who was a cultivated body and a chip, and who knew what it is to be an order placed in a house, spoke quietly:
blocks.html: Aya, who was a cultivated body and a chip, and who knew what it is to be an order placed in a house, spoke quietly:

blocks.text: “I was manufactured once. I wasn't taken apart afterwards to be given a courtyard. They brought me whole, in a van, and the courtyard gradually made me. If they take you apart, even if they put you together well, I'll have a while of courtyard without you. That while doesn't travel. That while stays here, with me, and I don't know under what principle it's conserved. Nowhere, perhaps. In me.”

blocks.text: In the chip, Eva asked, and Aya said it aloud, so it would be on record in the kitchen:
blocks.html: In the chip, Eva asked, and Aya said it aloud, so it would be on record in the kitchen:

blocks.text: *If what travels is an order and what stays is a while, which is more of a life: the order that can be named, or the while that doesn't travel? And if nothing is lost, where is the fear kept of the woman who waits beside the empty chair?*
blocks.html: If what travels is an order and what stays is a while, which is more of a life: the order that can be named, or the while that doesn't travel? And if nothing is lost, where is the fear kept of the woman who waits beside the empty chair?

blocks.text: MAY, beside her:
blocks.html: MAY, beside her:

blocks.text: *The one who searches has described a transfer of order, not of a bundle. The original does not remain. There is an interval in which the body is not a place. Nuria called it a hollow. That is the fact.*
blocks.html: The one who searches has described a transfer of order, not of a bundle. The original does not remain. There is an interval in which the body is not a place. Nuria called it a hollow. That is the fact.

blocks.text: The next day Andrés went to see the machine at El Estacio, alone, without crossing. He stood in front of the circle, the way you stand in front of a sea that isn't yours. The technician, discreet, didn't push him. He showed him, on a screen, the record of the cup and of Nuria, some curves that told Andrés as little as a company report and, at the same time, too much: there, reduced to a name, was the order of a woman who had cried when she tasted the salt.

blocks.text: “If I went in,” he asked, “who can assure me that what comes out on the other side still loves this cup, and not another, smoother one?”
blocks.html: “If I went in,” he asked, “who can assure me that what comes out on the other side still loves this cup, and not another, smoother one?”

blocks.text: The technician, honest or tired, shrugged.
blocks.html: The technician, honest or tired, shrugged.

blocks.text: “Nobody can fully assure you. So far the machine gets right what we measure. What we don't measure (the loving, the fear, the way of saying a daughter's name) doesn't show up in the curve. It shows up, if it does, in the mouth of the one who arrives, when you ask them.”

blocks.text: Andrés walked home along the promenade, like Raúl on the day he came down for the first time in years. The water was copper-coloured. He told himself, not through the bridge but to himself, that he wouldn't go in yet. That if anyone crossed toward here, he would let it be the other one, the one who had already left once, the one who knew how to leave. He knew how to stay. Staying, now, also meant not stepping into a circle.

blocks.text: Lía was waiting for him on the doorstep, the slow clock behind her, and didn't ask him for a hero's decision.
blocks.html: Lía was waiting for him on the doorstep, the slow clock behind her, and didn't ask him for a hero's decision.

blocks.text: “It's all right not to go in today,” she said. “A phrase doesn't deserve a whole father in the first month. Let the machine work, if it works, with those who ask. For now, you be a place. I need a place. So does Mother.”

blocks.text: He nodded, and at night he dreamed of a circle that was a plate, and of himself, dismantled, turned into water, and the Mar Menor receiving him without questions. He woke with dry sheets and Aya's hand on his side, real, present, not named in any curve. He lay very still, being a place, and that stillness seemed to him, that night, the most exact way of not getting lost, even though the phrase, in the hangar and in the warehouse, still said that nothing, ever, is lost.
